slides.title: What is a Data Structure?
slides.content:
# Data Structures 📊

## Definition

A data structure is a way to organize and store data for efficient access and modification.

## Types of Data Structures

```
Data Structures
├── Linear
│   ├── Arrays
│   ├── Linked Lists
│   ├── Stacks
│   └── Queues
└── Non-Linear
    ├── Trees
    ├── Graphs
    └── Hash Tables
```

## Choosing the Right One

| Need | Data Structure |
|------|---------------|
| Fast lookup by index | Array |
| Fast insert/delete | Linked List |
| LIFO operations | Stack |
| FIFO operations | Queue |
| Fast lookup by key | Hash Table |
| Hierarchical data | Tree |
| Networks/relationships | Graph |

> 🎯 **The right data structure makes code 100x faster!**

slides.title: Time and Space Complexity
slides.content:
# Complexity Analysis ⏱️

## Time Complexity

How runtime grows with input size:

```python
# O(1) - Constant time
def get_first(arr):
    return arr[0]  # Always 1 operation

# O(n) - Linear time
def find_item(arr, item):
    for x in arr:  # n operations (worst case)
        if x == item:
            return True
    return False

# O(n²) - Quadratic time
def bubble_sort(arr):
    for i in range(len(arr)):      # n times
        for j in range(len(arr)):  # n times each
            # Compare and swap
```

## Space Complexity

How memory grows with input size:

```python
# O(1) - Constant space
def sum_array(arr):
    total = 0  # Only 1 variable
    for x in arr:
        total += x
    return total

# O(n) - Linear space
def copy_array(arr):
    new_arr = arr.copy()  # New array of size n
    return new_arr
```

> 💡 **We care about worst-case complexity!**

slides.title: Big-O Notation
slides.content:
# Big-O Notation 📈

## Common Complexities (Best to Worst)

```
O(1)       Constant     → Hash table lookup
O(log n)   Logarithmic  → Binary search
O(n)       Linear       → Simple search
O(n log n) Linearithmic → Merge sort
O(n²)      Quadratic    → Nested loops
O(2ⁿ)      Exponential  → Recursive fibonacci
O(n!)      Factorial    → Permutations
```

## Visual Comparison (n = 1000)

| Complexity | Operations | Time (1μs/op) |
|------------|------------|---------------|
| O(1) | 1 | 1 μs |
| O(log n) | 10 | 10 μs |
| O(n) | 1,000 | 1 ms |
| O(n log n) | 10,000 | 10 ms |
| O(n²) | 1,000,000 | 1 second |
| O(2ⁿ) | 10^301 | Heat death of universe |

## Big-O Rules

```python
# Drop constants
O(2n) → O(n)
O(100) → O(1)

# Keep dominant term
O(n² + n) → O(n²)
O(n + log n) → O(n)
```

> 🎯 **Big-O describes the growth rate, not exact time!**

slides.title: Algorithm Efficiency
slides.content:
# Measuring Efficiency 🏎️

## Same Problem, Different Speeds

```python
# Find if number exists in sorted array

# O(n) - Linear Search
def linear_search(arr, target):
    for x in arr:
        if x == target:
            return True
    return False

# O(log n) - Binary Search (much faster!)
def binary_search(arr, target):
    left, right = 0, len(arr) - 1
    while left <= right:
        mid = (left + right) // 2
        if arr[mid] == target:
            return True
        elif arr[mid] < target:
            left = mid + 1
        else:
            right = mid - 1
    return False
```

## Real Impact

| Array Size | Linear Search | Binary Search |
|------------|---------------|---------------|
| 1,000 | 1,000 ops | 10 ops |
| 1,000,000 | 1,000,000 ops | 20 ops |
| 1 billion | 1 billion ops | 30 ops |

> 💡 **Algorithm choice matters more than hardware!**

slides.title: Trade-offs in Design
slides.content:
# Space vs Time Trade-offs ⚖️

## The Fundamental Trade-off

```
Faster algorithms often use more memory.
Memory-efficient algorithms are often slower.
```

## Examples

### Hash Table (Trade space for time)

```python
# O(n) space, O(1) lookup
lookup = {item: index for index, item in enumerate(items)}

# vs O(1) space, O(n) lookup
for i, item in enumerate(items):
    if item == target:
        return i
```

### Caching/Memoization

```python
# Without cache: O(2ⁿ) time, O(n) space
def fib(n):
    if n <= 1: return n
    return fib(n-1) + fib(n-2)

# With cache: O(n) time, O(n) space
from functools import lru_cache

@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def fib(n):
    if n <= 1: return n
    return fib(n-1) + fib(n-2)
```

## Choosing the Right Trade-off

| Constraint | Optimize For |
|------------|-------------|
| Limited memory (embedded) | Space |
| Speed critical (realtime) | Time |
| Neither | Balance / Readability |

> 🎯 **Know your constraints before optimizing!**

slides.title: Summary
slides.content:
# Excellent Work! 🎉

You've learned DSA fundamentals!

## Definition and Importance
- ✅ DSA = Efficient problem solving
- ✅ Critical for interviews and career

## Time and Space Complexity
- ✅ Time = How runtime grows
- ✅ Space = How memory grows

## Big-O Notation
- ✅ O(1) < O(log n) < O(n) < O(n log n) < O(n²)
- ✅ Drop constants and lower terms
- ✅ Focus on worst case

## Algorithm Efficiency
- ✅ Choice of algorithm > Hardware
- ✅ Binary search beats linear search

## Trade-offs
- ✅ Space vs Time trade-off
- ✅ Caching trades memory for speed
- ✅ Know your constraints

## Complexity Cheat Sheet

```
O(1)       → Hash table, array access
O(log n)   → Binary search
O(n)       → Linear search
O(n log n) → Merge sort, quick sort
O(n²)      → Bubble sort, nested loops
```
